findings.obs_text: In Pro 24:32 the watcher saw and considered the sluggard's field, set his heart on it, and received instruction: considering is the step between seeing and being taught. In Ecc 12:9 the Preacher's weighing of proverbs is part of his teaching the people knowledge. In 1Ti 6:1 servants count masters worthy of honor so that the teaching is not reviled.
In Ecc 3:18 with regard to links the Preacher's word in his heart to the children of man, whom God is testing so that they see they are like beasts.

In Job 34:27 the ones who turned aside from following God had no regard for his ways: the turning aside and the lack of regard are one fault. In Eze 18:28 the man considered and turned away from his transgressions: the considering leads the turning. In Isa 29:17 turned is Lebanon made a field, and regarded is the field counted as a forest.
findings.grounds: had no regard for any of his ways

findings.obs_text: In Rom 2:26 the uncircumcised man who keeps the law's precepts has his uncircumcision counted as circumcision: the counting reckons a state as its opposite on the ground of keeping.
findings.grounds: keeps the precepts of the law

findings.obs_text: In Job 1:8 and Job 2:3 the Lord asks Satan whether he has set his heart on Job, and names Job blameless and upright: the considering is turned to a man whose uprightness the Lord states.
findings.grounds: Have you considered my servant Job

findings.obs_text: In 2Th 3:15 the believers are told not to count the disobedient man an enemy but to warn him as a brother: how he is regarded decides how he is warned.
In Deu 33:9 the Levite who regards not father and mother is the one who observed the Lord's word: withholding regard from kin stands with watching over the word.

older.finding: How it co-exists. The test is passed by putting God above kin: Levi "said of his father and mother, 'I regard them not'; he disowned his brothers and ignored his children. For they observed your word" (33:9). Contrast U1 §2 (KS), where kinship grounds the refusal of strife.
older.reason: it states how watch works in a person; the watch collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Deu 9:27 Moses asks the Lord not to regard the stubbornness of the people: the willful hardness is what he asks the Lord to look past.
findings.grounds: Do not regard the stubbornness of this people

findings.obs_text: In Job 37:24 God does not regard those wise in their own conceit. In Pro 17:28 the fool who keeps silent is counted wise and intelligent. In Ecc 12:9 the wise Preacher weighs proverbs. In Isa 29:16 the potter counted as clay is the reversal of the maker, said of those who claim he has no understanding. In Isa 53:8 judgment is what took the servant away while his generation did not consider it.
findings.grounds: Even a fool who keeps silent is considered wise

older.finding: Face: The potter's formed thing; Verses: Isa 29:16; What differs: The formed thing says of its former, "He has no understanding"; Why: Creature denies creator (S)
older.reason: it states a face or use of the wise words; the wise collection owns it
